turns.assessment: The failure is a unidirectional loss of all optical launch power on OMS S10->S02. Input power is lost even at the booster, while pump-current telemetry remains unchanged; the reverse OMS S02->S10 is normal. This localizes the cause ahead of the booster, strongly favoring a disconnected/broken OMS input patch at S10 over an amplifier failure or fibre cut.

proposals.rationale: A pulled input patch at S10 removes all channels before amp0, matching loss of amp0 input and output and the downstream losses at every amplifier and receiver. Normal pump currents and the unaffected reverse direction support this localization; recent maintenance at S10 adds support.

Failure of the S10 WSS port feeding the S02 degree could also block every channel before the booster, but there is no direct ROADM equipment alarm and the maintenance-associated patch fault is more likely.
The location fits, but contamination normally causes reduced power rather than the complete signal loss observed across all channels.
A failed booster could remove downstream output, but it would not explain loss of the booster's own input power, and its pump-current telemetry did not change.
